chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, from Abdul Wahid ibn Al-Mukhtar Al-Ansary, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abdul Wahid! It would not harm a man when he was upon that view (of al-Wilayah), whatever the people say for him, and even if they were to say he was insane; and it would not harm him, even if he was at the top of a mountain worshipping Allah until the death comes to him.'

key_terms.الرَّأْيِ: the view/conviction — refers in context to the firm doctrinal belief in al-Wilayah, the guardianship and authority of the Imams (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.النَّاسُ: the people — the general public or opponents who pass judgment, criticize, or mock the believer
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death — the natural end of earthly life, until which the believer's worship and steadfastness must endure
key_terms.رَأْسِ جَبَلٍ: the top of a mountain — a rhetorical image of complete solitude and withdrawal from society, emphasizing that the believer's worth is independent of social acceptance
key_terms.مَجْنُونٌ: insane/mad — the most extreme derogatory label that opponents or the general public may apply to a committed holder of al-Wilayah
key_terms.يَضُرُّ: it harms — the verb negated twice in the hadith to categorically deny that social condemnation or isolation can cause any true harm to the steadfast believer
key_terms.يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ: worshipping Allah — continuous, sincere devotion to God, presented here as the sole sufficient occupation of the believer's life

ai.seo_question: Does it harm a believer who holds firm to al-Wilayah when people mock or accuse him of being insane?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) reassures 'Abd al-Wahid that a believer who holds firmly to the conviction of al-Wilayah — the guardianship and authority of the Imams — suffers no true harm from the ridicule, condemnation, or accusations of insanity levelled at him by people. The Imam extends this principle to its furthest limit, affirming that even complete social isolation — worshipping Allah alone atop a mountain until death arrives — is entirely sufficient for such a believer, making the verdict of society spiritually irrelevant.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, from Abdul Wahid Bin Al Mukhtar Al Ansary who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abdul Wahid! It would not harm a man when he was upon that view (of Al-Wilayah), what the people say for him, and even if they were to say he was insane; and it would not harm him and even if he was at the top of the mountain worshipping Allah<sup>azwj</sup> until the death comes to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Fudayl ibn Yasar from ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn al- Mukhtar al-Ansari who has said the following: “Once

abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to me, ‘O ‘Abd al-Wahid, nothing can harm one, if he is a person of proper understanding, who believes in our (Divine Authority), no matter what people may say about him. Although they may call him insane it will not harm him even if he lives on a mountain worshipping Allah until death approaches him.’”
